No static JSON corpus (2,047 battle + 747 support + 43 item collision entries, 311 jpower attack rows, chr_b.json) encodes runtime pool/entity state, so nothing in the data can contradict a generic fixed-slot free-list allocator. No data implication; UPHELD on absence of contradiction.

Destroy primitive symmetric to the Q1 alloc claim (same manager +0xc active-list / +0x1c retire-list pair, same 0x2037c24/0x2037b98 utilities); '32 call sites' is a static call-graph fact, not something any collision/jpower/chr_b JSON field encodes. Independently reloaded all 281 collision JSONs: merged nonzero ProjectileId set across 2,794 entries (2,047 battle + 747 support) has exactly 26 distinct values (matches round-2's 15 battle / 25 support counts), and value 2 is NEVER among them -- while collisionType==2 occurs 240/2,047 times in battle and 13/747 in support. This corroborates, not contradicts, the claim's own hedge that the case-9 '+0x1b==2' comparison is a move-kind/collisionType-like enum rather than literal on-disk ProjectileId (CollisionEntry.cs offset +3). Also, offsets +0x1a/+0x1b exceed CollisionEntry.EntrySize=20 bytes, structurally ruling out a direct 1:1 map onto the raw 20-byte disk record, consistent with the claim's own 'nested sub-object' framing.

Ownership back-pointer claim (wrapper+0xc holds the MoveInfo pointer) describes a runtime struct layout with no counterpart in any exported JSON (collision entries and jpower rows are static authored per-move data, not live MoveInfo/wrapper instances). No data field exists to confirm or refute a specific in-memory offset. No data implication; UPHELD by default (no contradiction found).

No static data corpus captures per-entity runtime lifetime/position state, so nothing can contradict these numbers. UPHELD on data grounds only.
